narrative:
The model determined that you have a 59% chance of representing a bad credit risk. Because this probability is above the approval threshold, your loan application was denied.

The three factors that most strongly shaped this outcome were the status of your checking account, the length of the loan you requested, and the amount in your savings. Your checking account being in negative balance (<0 DM) was the single biggest reason for the rejection. Among approved applicants, only 12.6% have a negative balance while nearly 60% have no checking account at all; this status strongly pushed the prediction toward bad credit risk.

The 12-month duration you asked for worked in your favor. Approved loans average 19 months, so the shorter term helped pull the prediction back toward approval. Unfortunately this positive effect was not large enough to overcome the other factors.

Your low savings balance (<100 DM) also increased the risk score. This is a common situation (46% of applicants are in the same bracket), but in combination with the negative checking account it added further weight toward denial.

You should focus on two practical steps. First, bring your checking account back into positive territory and begin building at least 500 DM in savings. Second, consider applying again in a few months with an even shorter loan term if possible. These changes would directly address the main reasons the application was turned down today.
